claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has superior plastic strain and toughness to commercially pure tungsten during high-temperature service.
Enhanced lattice distortion causes the proposed improvement in plastic strain and toughness.
A refined, heterogeneous grain structure causes the proposed improvement in plastic strain and toughness.
The proposed microstructure impedes dislocation motion.
The proposed microstructure facilitates grain-boundary sliding.
The proposed microstructural state increases energy absorption and delays failure under plasma-facing-component conditions.
The initial arc-melted equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy has a homogeneous single-phase microstructure.
Repeated arc melting produces a well-mixed, homogeneous WTaTiVZr alloy.
Mechanical loading at 1200°C to 1500°C and the proposed strain rates are representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
Equimolar mixing of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr creates significant lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr leads to a fine, heterogeneous grain structure.
The refined microstructure suppresses localized dislocation movement and promotes distributed deformation through grain-boundary sliding.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have statistically significantly greater strain-to-failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will absorb more tensile-test energy than pure tungsten.
The proposed mechanism is applicable approximately from 1200°C to 1500°C but may not apply at lower temperatures or to other HEA compositions.
W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr constitute a set of low-activation refractory elements.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described broadly as having a homogeneous microstructure, whereas the causal explanation relies on a fine, heterogeneous grain structure. These could be reconciled if 'homogeneous' refers only to phase or composition, but that distinction is not stated.

The initial comparison uses commercially pure tungsten processed under standard conditions, while the falsification experiment requires tungsten and the HEA to undergo identical arc-melting and processing protocols. These define materially different controls.
